transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess the main thing is my eating’s been really off lately. Like some days before work I’ll just have coffee and maybe a granola bar, and then I’m already halfway through a shift before I realize I haven’t really eaten. I work in healthcare support, so you’d think I’d be better about that, but the break room’s always got those vending machine snacks and people arguing about whose lunch is whose... anyway, my scrubs have started hanging kind of loose on me, and I’m not trying to lose weight or anything. It’s been worrying me.
Have you been trying to lose weight?

No, not at all. I mean, if anything I forget to eat, or I’ll think I ate more than I did because I had coffee and a granola bar, but that’s not really a meal. Then I’m on my feet at work and suddenly my scrubs are loose, and I’m like… okay, that’s not something I was aiming for.
Have you noticed any changes in your interest in activities you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I guess I have. I used to run in Van Cortlandt Park, and I’d take my camera out sometimes, get pictures of the trees or the tracks, whatever caught my eye. And I played chess with a couple friends too—nothing serious, just coffee and trash talk mostly.

Lately I keep telling myself there’s no point. Like I’ll think about going out, then I just… don’t. I end up at home scrolling on my phone or opening my budget spreadsheet again, which is ridiculous because the numbers don’t change just because I stare at them. But yeah, the things I used to like don’t really pull me in much right now.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time lately?

Yeah… most mornings, honestly. I wake up and there’s this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day’s already spoiled before I even get my work badge on. And then I’ll be brushing my teeth or looking for clean socks and thinking about stupid little things, like whether the train’s going to be delayed, but underneath it it’s just that same empty kind of weight.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything lately?

Yeah… I have. It’s not like one big thing I did, it’s more like everything feels like my fault. At the clinic, if a room turnover is late by a few minutes, I’ll be standing there thinking I messed up everyone’s whole day, like the nurse is behind now, the patient’s annoyed, the doctor’s schedule is off, and it’s because of me.

And then I go home and it’s the same kind of thought with my family, like I’m just… extra weight for them to deal with. Which sounds dramatic when I say it out loud, because people make small mistakes all the time. I know that. But in my head it turns into this whole thing, like I’m a burden and I should’ve done better.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It’s been… a while. Not forever, I guess. The really steady part, where it’s like the sadness and not wanting to do things kind of settled in and stayed, that’s been maybe about a year and four months.

I remember because I kept thinking it was just a bad stretch, like when the seasons change or when work gets annoying, but then months kept stacking up. So… yeah, roughly sixteen months, something like that.
Have you experienced any periods where your symptoms were significantly worse than they are now?

Yeah… there have been stretches where it’s worse than this. Like, when the depression really drops down, it’s not just me feeling low. The voices are still there too, and that feeling like people are tracking my charting, like they’re watching what I put in the system.

It gets hard at work because I’m trying to do my shift and keep up with rooms and notes and everything, and at the same time I’m fighting that heavy mood and trying not to react to the voices or that watched feeling. Sometimes I’ll be looking at a screen and I can’t even tell if I’m being careful or if I’m stuck on it too long, you know? So… yeah, the worst periods are when both things are happening together.
Have you had more than one episode of feeling this low in your life?

I’m not totally sure how to count that, honestly. Like… there have been bad times before, but when you say “episode,” I don’t know if you mean like a clear start and stop, because mine doesn’t always feel that neat.

I can remember times where I was lower than usual, but then I start thinking, well, was that actually separate or was I just busy with work and not paying attention? Like sometimes at the clinic you just keep going because there’s rooms to turn over and people needing things, and you don’t really sit there measuring your mood like a thermometer.

So… I don’t know. Maybe? But I can’t give you a clean number.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy, irritable, or had a lot of energy?

I don’t know… I mean, I’ve had days where I’m more keyed up or irritated, sure, but “extremely happy” or like a bunch of energy? I’m not sure I’d call it that.

Sometimes at work there’s just a rush, you know, like everyone’s asking for something and the phones are going and you kind of move fast because you have to. But that’s not really the same thing as feeling amazing or anything. I guess I’d need you to say what you mean by “a period,” because I’m not sure I’ve noticed something like that.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or had a lot of energy that lasted for several days?

Several days… I don’t know. I can’t really think of a stretch like that where I was extremely happy or had all this energy for days. I mean, sometimes I’ll get a lot done if there’s stuff piled up, like errands or work things, but that feels more like pressure than feeling good.

I guess I’d say I haven’t noticed that in a clear way. I’d have to think about it more, but nothing jumps out like that.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or irritable and had a lot of energy at the same time?

I’m not sure. I mean, irritable, yes, I’ve had that, but with a lot of energy at the same time… I don’t know if I’d put those together.

Sometimes I’ll be snapping at people in my head, like at work when someone leaves supplies in the wrong place and then you’re hunting for things, and it turns into this whole thing where you’re thinking, “Why can’t people just put stuff back?” But that’s more frustration than, like, having all this extra energy.

So… I don’t think I’ve noticed a clear period like that. Not one I could point to and say, yeah, that was definitely happening.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or irritable and your thoughts were racing at the same time?

Racing thoughts… I’m not sure. I mean, I get a lot on my mind sometimes, especially if there’s work stuff or, like, bills or something I forgot to do, and then it kind of jumps from one thing to the next.

But I don’t know if that’s the same as “racing.” And with being extremely happy or irritable at the same time… I mean, irritable maybe, but I can’t really point to a period where it all lined up like that. Sometimes I’m annoyed and my head feels busy, but then I’ll start thinking about something totally different, like whether I left my badge in the car or if I need to get gas, so it’s hard to say.

So… no clear period that I’ve noticed, I guess.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or extremely irritable and had a reduced need for sleep at the same time?

I don’t really know. I mean, I’ve had nights where I don’t sleep well, but that’s usually because my mind won’t settle or I’m thinking about the next day, like if I have to be up early for work or there’s something I forgot to do. 

But feeling extremely happy or extremely irritable and then not needing sleep… I’m not sure I’ve had that. Sometimes I’m tired but still have to get up and do things, you know, like when the laundry piles up or there’s stuff around the apartment that bothers me. But that’s not really the same as needing less sleep. So… I don’t think I can say yes to that.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or extremely irritable and your behavior changed in a way that was noticeable to others?

I’m not sure. I mean, people notice when I’m irritated sometimes, like if I’m quieter or I don’t want to talk much, but I don’t know if my behavior changed in some big way.

It’s hard to tell because at work, everybody kind of has days where they’re short with each other, especially when it gets busy or someone doesn’t do their part. Like there’s one supply room where things are never where they’re supposed to be, and then everyone’s blaming everyone else, and I might come off annoyed. But I don’t know if that’s what you mean.

I can’t really think of a period where I was extremely happy or extremely irritable and other people were saying I was acting different. Not that I remember, anyway.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or extremely irritable and acted in a way that was noticeably different from your normal behavior?

I don’t think so… not in a way that stands out to me. I mean, I have days where I’m more annoyed or I keep to myself more, but that feels kind of normal depending on what’s going on.

Like if work is chaotic, or if I’m running late and then I can’t find my keys, that can throw me off for the whole morning. And then I might be quieter or short with somebody, but I don’t know that anyone would say, “You’re acting really different.”

So… I’m not sure. I can’t really point to a period like that.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or extremely irritable and acted impulsively?

Impulsively… I don’t know. I mean, I’ve bought things I probably didn’t need, like little stuff for the apartment or food when I should’ve cooked, but I don’t think that was because I was extremely happy or angry or anything.

Sometimes when I’m irritated I’ll leave a conversation or just go for a walk, but that’s more like trying not to make it worse. At work, you kind of have to keep it together anyway, because if you snap at the wrong person then it becomes this whole thing, and then the schedule gets messed up, and everybody remembers it.

So… no, I can’t really think of a time like that. Not where I was in some mood and acting really impulsive.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or extremely irritable and acted in a way that got you into trouble or caused problems for you or others?

I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve gotten irritated and maybe been a little short with people, but I can’t think of a time where it got me into real trouble or caused some big problem.

Like at work, if someone leaves equipment in the wrong place or doesn’t restock something, it can make the whole shift harder, and people get tense. I might complain or be quiet for a while, but I usually try not to let it turn into anything. It’s not like I got written up or had some huge fight because of it.

So… no, not that I can remember.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or irritable and acted in a way that was noticeably different from your normal behavior for several days or longer?

Several days or longer… I don’t really think so. I mean, I can get in a mood, sure, but it’s usually tied to something, like a bad shift or not sleeping right or somebody being careless with supplies. That can stick with me for a day, maybe I’ll be quieter or kind of tense.

But several days where I’m acting noticeably different… I don’t know. Nobody’s really said that to me, at least not that I remember. Sometimes coworkers notice if you’re off, but then again everybody’s off sometimes in that job, so it’s hard to tell what counts.

So I guess no, not that I’ve noticed.
Have you had two weeks or more in a row where you felt sad or empty most of the time?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, two weeks sounds very specific, but it’s been stretches like that where most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day’s already ruined before I even put on my badge.

And then I’ll still get up and do what I’m supposed to do, because you have to, you know—people are waiting, the floor doesn’t run itself, somebody’s always asking where something is. But that feeling is there before any of that even starts. It’s not just a bad morning here and there.
Have you had two weeks or more in a row where you felt sad or empty most of the time, consistently, without any breaks?

Yeah… I mean, “without any breaks” is hard for me to say perfectly, because I’m not writing it down day by day or anything. But there have been stretches where most mornings I wake up with that same heavy, hollow feeling, like the day’s already ruined before I even put on my badge.

It’s not like I wake up and think, “Oh, today’s fine,” and then something happens. It’s already there. Some mornings maybe it’s a little less sharp, I guess, but it’s still kind of sitting there. So… yeah, most of the time during those stretches.

At work, you kind of have to keep it together anyway, because if you snap at the wrong person then it becomes this whole thing, and then the schedule gets messed up, and everybody remembers it.

So… no, I can’t really think of a time like that. Not where I was in some mood and acting really impulsive.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a manic or hypomanic episode
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or extremely irritable and acted in a way that got you into trouble or caused problems for you or others?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about manic or hypomanic episodes—periods of extremely elevated or irritable mood with behavior causing trouble or problems—which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve gotten irritated and maybe been a little short with people, but I can’t think of a time where it got me into real trouble or caused some big problem.

Like at work, if someone leaves equipment in the wrong place or doesn’t restock something, it can make the whole shift harder, and people get tense. I might complain or be quiet for a while, but I usually try not to let it turn into anything. It’s not like I got written up or had some huge fight because of it.

So… no, not that I can remember.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's symptoms meet the criteria for a manic episode
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or irritable and acted in a way that was noticeably different from your normal behavior for several days or longer?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about possible manic or hypomanic episodes—periods of elevated or irritable mood with noticeably different behavior lasting several days or longer—which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
Several days or longer… I don’t really think so. I mean, I can get in a mood, sure, but it’s usually tied to something, like a bad shift or not sleeping right or somebody being careless with supplies. That can stick with me for a day, maybe I’ll be quieter or kind of tense.

But several days where I’m acting noticeably different… I don’t know. Nobody’s really said that to me, at least not that I remember. Sometimes coworkers notice if you’re off, but then again everybody’s off sometimes in that job, so it’s hard to tell what counts.

So I guess no, not that I’ve noticed.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the criteria for a major depressive episode
doctor.question: Have you had two weeks or more in a row where you felt sad or empty most of the time?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge.
target_item.reason: The question is directly asking about a sustained period of feeling sad or empty most of the time, which matches depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. I mean, two weeks sounds very specific, but it’s been stretches like that where most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day’s already ruined before I even put on my badge.

And then I’ll still get up and do what I’m supposed to do, because you have to, you know—people are waiting, the floor doesn’t run itself, somebody’s always asking where something is. But that feeling is there before any of that even starts. It’s not just a bad morning here and there.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the duration criteria for a major depressive episode
doctor.question: Have you had two weeks or more in a row where you felt sad or empty most of the time, consistently, without any breaks?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a sustained period of feeling sad or empty most of the time, which directly corresponds to depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, “without any breaks” is hard for me to say perfectly, because I’m not writing it down day by day or anything. But there have been stretches where most mornings I wake up with that same heavy, hollow feeling, like the day’s already ruined before I even put on my badge.

It’s not like I wake up and think, “Oh, today’s fine,” and then something happens. It’s already there. Some mornings maybe it’s a little less sharp, I guess, but it’s still kind of sitting there. So… yeah, most of the time during those stretches.
